learn.hook: Can your hands dance? Let us say a rhyme and move them!
points: A rhyme is a short poem with a fun beat.
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words.
Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
We say a rhyme slowly and clearly, with a happy voice.

example.q: Read the rhyme: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap. Tap your knees, tap, tap, tap. Up they go and down they go. Wave to friends and say hello!" Which word rhymes with clap?
steps: Say clap. It ends with the sound -ap.
Say tap. It also ends with -ap.
So clap and tap rhyme.

learn.reallife: We say action rhymes in the school assembly and at home with Nani and Dadi.

items.text: Up they go and ___ they go.

games.title: True or false?
items: Clap and tap are rhyming words.
Go and hello are rhyming words.
Hand and cat are rhyming words.
Hand ends with -and. Cat ends with -at.
In an action rhyme, we move as we say it.
We do the actions, like clapping and waving.
In the rhyme, the hands say goodbye.
The hands wave and say hello.

quiz.q: Read: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap." What do the hands do?
quiz.explain: The line says the hands go clap, clap, clap.
steps: Read the line: clap your hands, clap, clap, clap.
The action word is clap.
So the hands clap.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the action word in the line

quiz.q: Read: "Wave to friends and say hello!" What do we say to friends?
steps: Read the line: wave to friends and say hello.
The word after say is hello.
So we say hello.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.explain: Tap and map both end with the sound -ap.
steps: Say tap. It ends with -ap.
Say map. It also ends with -ap.
So map rhymes with tap. Top starts like tap but ends with -op.
quiz.mistake: Thinks words that start the same will rhyme

quiz.explain: Go and no both end with the sound -o.
steps: Say go. It ends with -o.
Say no. It also ends with -o.
So no rhymes with go. Got ends with -ot.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first letter, not the ending sound

quiz.q: Read: "Up they go and down they go." Which word is the opposite of up?
steps: Up means high. The line says up they go and down they go.
Down means low.
So the opposite of up is down.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the opposite of up

quiz.q: How many hands do we clap together?
quiz.explain: We clap two hands together. One hand cannot clap on its own.
steps: We have two hands.
We clap them together.
So we clap 2 hands.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of hands with fingers

teach.ask: Gappu: What is an action rhyme? How do I say one?
teach.praise: Clap, clap! Now I can say an action rhyme!
teach.nudge: What do we do with our hands while we say the rhyme?

revise.summary: An action rhyme is a short, fun poem. We do the actions as we say it. Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
focus: Read a line and find the action in it
Find words that rhyme by their ending sound
Say a rhyme slowly and clearly
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound: clap, tap, map; go, no
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words
traps: Don't look at the first letter to find a rhyme. Look at the ending sound.
Top does not rhyme with tap. Map does.

learn.hook: Your body is like a busy team. Each part has a job!
points: We see with our eyes and hear with our ears.
We smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
We hold things with our hands and walk with our legs.
We have one nose, two eyes, two ears and two hands.

example.q: Think it through: I want to smell a rose. Which body part do I use?
steps: Smelling is the job of the nose.
Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells.
So I use my nose.

learn.reallife: When we wash up in the morning, we clean our face, eyes, ears, hands and feet.

games.title: Match the part to its job

quiz.q: Which body part do we use to see a kite?
quiz.explain: We see things with our eyes.
steps: Eyes see. Ears hear. Nose smells.
To see a kite, we use our eyes.

quiz.q: Meena hears a bird sing. Which part helps her hear?
quiz.explain: We hear sounds with our ears.
steps: Hearing is the job of the ears.
So Meena hears the bird with her ears.

quiz.q: How many noses do you have?
quiz.explain: We have just one nose, in the middle of the face.
steps: Touch your face. There is one nose in the middle.
So we have 1 nose. We have two eyes, but only one nose.
quiz.mistake: Thinks we have two of every body part

quiz.q: 🖐️ Which is the right spelling for this body part?
steps: Say the sounds: h-a-n-d.
Put them in order: hand.
Hnad has the n and a mixed up. Hend has e in place of a.
Answer: hand
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of letters

quiz.explain: Nose begins with the sound n, so the letter is n.
steps: Say nose. The first sound is n.
So nose begins with n, not m.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the letters n and m

quiz.q: Which body part tastes a sweet laddoo?
quiz.explain: We taste food with our tongue.
steps: We taste food with our tongue.
So the tongue tastes the sweet laddoo.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which part tastes

teach.ask: Gappu: I have so many body parts! What do they all do?
teach.praise: Wow! Now I know my eyes see and my ears hear!
teach.nudge: What do eyes and ears do?

revise.summary: Each body part has a job. We see with our eyes, hear with our ears, smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
focus: Match each body part to its job
Know how many of each part we have
Spell body words like hand and nose
remember: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes
One nose, two eyes, two ears, two hands
traps: Don't think we have two of every part. We have only one nose.
Don't mix up seeing (eyes) with hearing (ears).

learn.hook: Jump! Run! Clap! These words make you move!
points: Some words tell us what we do. They are action words, or doing words.
Run, jump, clap, eat, sleep and write are action words.
We write with our hands. We kick with our feet.
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.

example.q: Think it through: In "Ravi kicks the ball", which is the action word?
steps: Ask: what does Ravi do?
Ravi kicks.
So kicks is the action word.

learn.reallife: In PT class, the teacher says: run, jump, stop! These are action words.

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

items.q: With a ball and your feet, you ___
With a glass of milk, you ___
With two hands at a show, you ___

quiz.explain: Jump tells us what we do. Hand is a body part. Red is a colour.
steps: An action word tells what we do.
We can jump. So jump is an action word.
Hand is a body part. Red is a colour.
Answer: Jump
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word instead of a doing word

quiz.q: Read: "Asha claps her hands." Which word is the action word?
steps: Ask: what does Asha do?
Asha claps. So claps is the action word.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word instead of the action

quiz.q: What do we do with a pencil?
quiz.explain: We hold a pencil and write with it.
steps: We hold a pencil in our hand.
We write with a pencil.
quiz.mistake: Matches the wrong action to the thing

quiz.explain: We brush our teeth every morning.
steps: Every morning we clean our teeth.
We brush our teeth. So the word is brush.
quiz.mistake: Picks an action that does not fit the sentence

quiz.q: Which action do we do with our legs?
quiz.explain: We run with our legs. We eat with our mouth and hear with our ears.
steps: Our legs help us move.
We run with our legs. We eat with our mouth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which body part does the action

quiz.q: Which is NOT an action word?
quiz.explain: Chair is the name of a thing. Sing and hop are things we do.
steps: Sing and hop are things we do.
Chair is the name of a thing.
So chair is NOT an action word.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every word is an action word

teach.ask: Gappu: What is an action word? Is chair one?
teach.praise: Hop, hop! I know action words now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me some things we do, like run or jump?

revise.summary: Action words, or doing words, tell us what we do, like run, jump, clap, eat and write.
focus: Pick the action word in a sentence
Tell action words apart from naming words
Match an action to the body part that does it
remember: Action words: run, jump, clap, eat, sleep, write
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.
Ask 'What does he or she do?' to find the action word
traps: Don't pick a naming word like hand or chair as the action word.
Don't match the wrong body part: we write with hands, kick with feet.
